advisory: A finding aid for how a day is put together, and never an authority for what was celebrated. The rules here are transcribed from this repository's own collated publications; the competent particular calendar, a legitimate indult and the competent annual Ordo control an actual celebration. Precedence is one of five decisions, and this layer takes only that one and the orations that follow from it.

assignment.note: NUALC 19 runs the Triduum from the evening Mass of the Lord's Supper to Evening Prayer on Easter Sunday, so Easter Sunday is in place 1 and not in place 2.

The Chrism Mass is a second Mass of Thursday of Holy Week, said in the cathedral that morning, and it is never ranked against the Mass of the Lord's Supper: it competes for nothing and is displaced by nothing. It is filed here rather than in place 1 because NUALC 19 begins the Triduum at the evening Mass, and the Ordo lectionum agrees, printing it among the Lenten ferias at feria V Hebdomadae sanctae.
The Most Sacred Heart of Jesus is inscribed in the General Roman Calendar by rule and not by date, as Feria VI post dominicam secundam post Pentecosten, and is a solemnity at place 3 like any other.

Two obligatory memorials inscribed by rule rather than by date, so the dated rules below cannot reach them. The notification of 24 March 2018 makes the Monday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Mother of the Church, prevail over any other memorial of a saint or blessed on the day; that notification has not been read here and its refinement is not applied. The official notification of 8 December 1998 has been read and is applied by the occurrence-only reduction above: it makes the Immaculate Heart and a coinciding obligatory memorial both optional for that year.

bases.why: a further Mass the books appoint on a day whose identity is settled by something else. It occupies no row of the table, so it can neither take the day nor be displaced by it; it is offered beside the day's own Mass and is never ranked against it

citation_forms.IGMR: Institutio generalis Missalis Romani, the General Instruction of the Roman Missal
citation_forms.NUALC: Normae universales de anno liturgico et de calendario, printed in the Missal before the General Roman Calendar

code: Normae universales de anno liturgico et de calendario, 1969, with the Institutio generalis Missalis Romani

surviving_qualification.what: On the weekdays of Advent from 17 December, on the days within the Octave of the Nativity, and on the weekdays of Lent, the Mass is of the occurring liturgical day, but the Collect may be taken from a memorial inscribed that day in the General Roman Calendar - Ash Wednesday and the weekdays of Holy Week excepted. This is the postconciliar residue of what the older system called a commemoration. It substitutes one collect; it never adds a second.

commemoration.what: This rite does not commemorate. The 1962 apparatus of privileged and ordinary commemorations, ceilings and second and third collects has no counterpart here. A celebration that loses on the table is omitted for the year, and no oration of it is added to the Mass that displaced it.

edition: Missale Romanum, editio typica tertia 2008, reimpressio emendata 2008

omission.gloss: Everything else that lost is omitted for that year. Not anticipated, not deferred, not commemorated - omitted. Transfer does not reach downwards: nothing below a solemnity is ever moved by the general law.

reduction.what: An obligatory memorial that falls on a weekday of Lent is not omitted outright but kept as an optional memorial, and in practice survives as the collect IGMR 355 a permits.

anticipation.what: The one movement backwards in the system. Where 19 March is a day of precept and Saint Joseph meets Palm Sunday, the solemnity is anticipated to Saturday 18 March; where it is not of precept, the Episcopal Conference may instead move it outside Lent altogether.
anticipation.why_not: Both branches turn on whether the day is of precept in a particular territory, which this repository does not know.

destination.rule: the nearest day free of the days listed under table places 1 to 8
destination.why_not: The destination depends on the place of every following day and on whether another solemnity has already been moved onto it. This repository does not compute it. The destinations the article fixes by name are computed, because the article states them.

proper_seats.destination: the Monday after the Second Sunday of Easter
proper_seats.note: This is not the nearest free day and is not derived from the general rule; it is a specific disposition that overrides it.
proper_seats.when: 25 March falls on any day of Holy Week

sunday_rule.what: A solemnity occurring on a Sunday of Advent, Lent or Easter goes to the following Monday rather than to the nearest free day, except on Palm Sunday and Easter Sunday, where the general rule of NUALC 60 takes over.

appointed_mass.what: The Missal prints a proper formulary for this day in the Proper of Time, and IGMR 355 a presupposes it by directing that the Mass be of the occurring liturgical day.
appointed_mass.why_not: This index carries the Sundays, the solemnities and the days of the Triduum, so the day is constituted here and its formulary is not transcribed. The gap is the Missal's Proper of Time, not a rubric this repository has not read.

mass_choice_not_yet_expressible.also: Enumerating the permission instead is out of reach for a third reason. Rubric 3 b permits any of the thirty-four Ordinary Time Masses and this index carries thirty-two of them, ot-2 to ot-33, the formularies of weeks 1 and 34 having no Sunday to be inscribed at. Thirty-two arms would understate the rubric and say nothing about the understatement.

gaps.what: an arm cannot name a base that varies with the date
gaps.where: tools/calendar-rubrics, check_mass_choices, which requires every arm to declare takes mass with a key this calendar's index carries, or takes office_mass; and src/web/browser/liturgy/assembly-model.js, massChoicesFor, which resolves an arm to option.mass or, for office_mass, to the winner's OWN formulary
gaps.why_it_blocks: The base IGMR 363 names is the preceding Sunday, which is a different key on every date, and the two alternatives it names - another Sunday in Ordinary Time, a prayer for various needs - name no key at all. An implied weekday's formulary is borrowed or absent and never own, so an office_mass arm resolves to null, is dropped, and takes the entry below two options, where the model discards it without a word. Writing the arms as fixed keys would be making the choice the rubric declines to make.

gaps.what: a choice cannot be confined to one season
gaps.why_it_blocks: `when` gates on weekday, winner_basis and with_candidate. Its when.season test compares the entry's own season field to itself and never to the day's, and the day's season is not passed into the function at all, so a season gate would read as a filter and filter nothing. The only basis available here, place-13-weekday, is equally the basis of the ordinary weekdays of Advent, of Christmas Time and of Easter Time, where neither IGMR 363 nor rubric 3 b applies. An entry written today would offer Ordinary Time's Masses on an Advent weekday.

mass_choice_not_yet_expressible.so: Nothing is written rather than something wrong. The entry is owed when a base is emitted, and the shape it needs is a takes value naming that emitted base and a `when` that actually tests the day's season. Both are changes to tools shared with the other calendar and neither is made from this source.

oration_scope.chooses_no_basis: This index chooses no oration basis for any Ordinary Time weekday, and nothing here may be read as having chosen one. IGMR 363 gives the orations of the preceding Sunday BESIDE the orations of another Sunday in Ordinary Time and the prayers for various needs, and the Missal's own rubric 3 b before the Masses of Ordinary Time - In feriis vero quaelibet e 34 Missis dici potest, attenta utilitate pastorali fidelium - permits any of the thirty-four. Proximity appoints none of them. No mass in propers.yaml carries a takes_from at an Ordinary Time weekday's oration slots, at mass level or at proper level, and none may: a takes_from citation records the edition's own printed pointer at the day, and what IGMR 363 states is a general rubric. The scope above says which slots would cross over IF a base were emitted. It emits none and prefers none.

not_slots.why: Not among them, and no tool may guess it. In this index the slot stands on the five Sundays of Lent, on Palm Sunday and on Good Friday and on no Sunday in Ordinary Time, so a scope naming it would name a slot no base holds.

omits.what: The readings. IGMR 358 gives every weekday of the year the ferial Lectionary's own readings, which are not the preceding Sunday's, and they do not cross over with the orations.
omits.why_not: This index carries no ferial Lectionary entry for an Ordinary Time weekday, so the omission cannot yet point at the day's own key and has to reach the page as a stated reason instead. A day shown a collect and no gospel, saying nothing, asserts by silence that the Mass has no gospel - the same defect one size smaller. When the ferial entries exist this statement points at the day's own key and stops being a gap.

oration_scope.slots_why: Nothing else in this file answers which slots are orations. The `orations` block below says how many collects are SAID on a day, never which propers are orations, and reading it as the latter would be the first wrong turn. These three are also the oration slots the bases themselves actually hold: the thirty-two Ordinary Time Sunday formularies this calendar's index carries, ot-2 to ot-33, each hold Collect, Prayer over the Offerings and Prayer after Communion and no other oration. So the scope names slots the base is known to hold rather than slots the Missal is assumed to print.
oration_scope.what: IGMR 363 lends the ORATIONS of the preceding Sunday - praeter orationes dominicae praecedentis - and nothing else. The other calendar's RGMR 299 lends the whole Mass, and reading the two as one borrowing is the error this declaration exists to stop: a base carried unscoped would put the Sunday's First Reading and Gospel on every Ordinary Time weekday of the year, cleanly resolved, well formed and wrong.

appointed_mass.what: The one kind of day the reformed Missal prints no formulary for. IGMR 363 gives the orations of the preceding Sunday, and beside them the orations of another Sunday in Ordinary Time or one of the prayers for various needs; from those Masses the collect alone may always be taken. IGMR 355 c widens the choice further to an occurring optional memorial, a saint in the Martyrology, a Mass for various needs or a votive Mass. The readings are the ferial Lectionary's own, IGMR 358, and are not the preceding Sunday's.
appointed_mass.why_not: This index carries every Sunday in Ordinary Time, so the formulary IGMR 363 names as the base IS held - but it is held under a key that varies with the date, and nothing emits which Sunday governs which weekday for this calendar. tools/calendar-days has the machinery and refuses to run it here, on a comment reading "nothing there points a weekday at the preceding Sunday". IGMR 363, registered and read at the bytes, says praeter orationes dominicae praecedentis - besides the orations of the preceding Sunday - so something does. Emitting a ferial_formulary block for this calendar would close 72 of the 136 keyless dates of 2026 at one stroke; it is a change to a tool shared with the 1962 calendar and is not made from this source alone.
appointed_mass.would_be_a_mass_choice: Once a base is emitted, the two alternatives IGMR 363 states are a mass_choices entry and not a collision: the rubric orders them, the preceding Sunday first.

mass_category.assumed: the Mass of the occurring liturgical day

constituted_days.measured_over: 2026, through the browser's own model at src/web/browser/liturgy/assembly-model.js, one derivation per civil date
constituted_days.not_a_precedence_question: None of this changes which celebration wins on a date. A day with no formulary still competes, still ranks and still displaces or is displaced; what it cannot do is show a reader any words. Nothing above is emitted into the ranking.
constituted_days.splits_two_ways: Sixty-four of the 136 fall under a rule whose day the Missal prints a proper Mass for, and closing them means transcribing the Proper of Time's weekdays into the index - a transcription, not a rule. Seventy-two fall under ordinary-time-weekday, where the Missal prints nothing and IGMR 363 points the day at the preceding Sunday, whose formulary this index already holds; closing those means emitting which Sunday governs which weekday, which is one rule and no new text. The larger half of the gap is the cheaper half, and it was not visible until the census was taken.
constituted_days.what: A day this file constitutes and no formulary reaches. It is a different thing from a placeholder Mass and must not be counted with one: a placeholder has a formulary appointed and its text untranscribed, while these have no formulary appointed at all. Each implied rule above now carries `appointed_mass` saying which of the two it is.

not_tested.category: the choice among an optional memorial, the weekday, a saint in the Martyrology, a Mass for various needs and a votive Mass on a weekday in Ordinary Time
Masses for various needs and occasions

mass_category.warning: IGMR 355 adds two cautions that belong beside any choice: the priest is not to omit the assigned weekday readings frequently and without sufficient cause, and where the choice lies between a memorial of the general calendar and one of a diocesan or religious calendar, other things being equal the particular memorial is to be preferred.

not_decided_here: The national, diocesan, religious and church calendars laid over the General Roman Calendar, which change ranks upwards for the places that own them. Places 4, 8 and 11 of the table are therefore always empty here.

Whether the Ascension, the Body and Blood of Christ or the Epiphany is kept on its own day or on a Sunday. NUALC 7 assigns them to a Sunday only where the competent authority has so decided, and both forms are shown, tagged, with neither chosen.
Whether the Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary is available (NUALC 15), which turns on whether an obligatory memorial occurs.
Which optional memorial a celebrant keeps where several fall on one day (NUALC 14; IGMR 355).
The Gloria, the Creed, the readings, the Preface, the Eucharistic Prayer and the colour.
Whether a solemnity transferred from an earlier date occupies this one, except at the Annunciation's named seat.

general_rule_not_collated.what: The General Instruction states the one-oration rule directly at its n. 54, and that article is the citation a reader should follow. This repository has not read n. 54 in a witness, so the count above is stated from NUALC 60 and IGMR 355 a, which it has read. The gap is recorded rather than papered over with a citation nobody here has checked.

memorial_orations.what: On a memorial the proper collect is said, or one from the appropriate Common; the other orations may be taken from the Common or from the current weekday.

orations.what: One collect. The number never varies with the day, because nothing is ever added to it: a losing celebration is omitted rather than commemorated (NUALC 60), and the one qualification the system carries - the collect of a memorial on a privileged weekday, IGMR 355 a - replaces the day's collect rather than following it.

overrides.locus: CDWDS, Notification Prot. n. 2671/98/L, 8 December 1998; Notitiae 35 (1999), 157
overrides.why: When the movable obligatory memorial of the Immaculate Heart coincides with another obligatory memorial, both are retained as optional memorials for that year.

concurrence.gloss: Where the Vespers of the current day and the First Vespers of the next meet, the higher place wins and a tie goes to the current day. It is stated for the Office and has no Mass analogue.

precedence.gloss: Unice - solely. There is no residual customary precedence, no appeal to the dignity of a titular, and no general principle that a solemnity always wins. Where two celebrations fall on one day the question is only which of them stands higher in the thirteen numbered places.

occurrence.gloss: Four dispositions in one article: occurrence resolved by the table; transfer, reserved to solemnities; the Annunciation's fixed transfer; and omission of everything else. Confusing them is the commonest error in calendar work.

rows.label: The Paschal Triduum of the Passion and Resurrection of the Lord

The Nativity, the Epiphany, the Ascension and Pentecost; the Sundays of Advent, Lent and Easter; Ash Wednesday; the weekdays of Holy Week from Monday to Thursday inclusive; the days within the Octave of Easter
rows.note: Ash Wednesday and the Holy Week weekdays outrank every solemnity, and so does a weekday of the Easter octave.

rows.label: Solemnities of the Lord, of the Blessed Virgin Mary and of the saints inscribed in the General Roman Calendar; the Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed

Proper solemnities: the principal patron of the place; the dedication and its anniversary for one's own church; the title of one's own church; the title, founder or principal patron of an Order or Congregation
Feasts of the Lord inscribed in the General Roman Calendar
rows.note: These, and only these, displace a Sunday of Christmas Time or of Ordinary Time.

rows.label: The Sundays of Christmas Time and the Sundays in Ordinary Time
Feasts of the Blessed Virgin Mary and of the saints in the General Roman Calendar
rows.note: Being below place 6, such a feast is simply omitted in a year in which it falls on a Sunday.

rows.label: Proper feasts: the diocesan principal patron; the cathedral dedication anniversary; the patron of a region, province, nation or wider territory; a religious title, founder or principal patron; other feasts proper to a church; other feasts of a diocesan or religious calendar
The privileged weekdays: Advent from 17 to 24 December inclusive, the days within the Octave of the Nativity, and the weekdays of Lent
rows.note: They stand above every memorial and below every feast.

rows.label: Obligatory memorials of the General Roman Calendar
Proper obligatory memorials: secondary patrons, and other obligatory memorials of a diocesan or religious calendar
Optional memorials
rows.note: The only entry in the table that carries a substantive rule inside it. Optional memorials may be made even on the privileged weekdays of place 9, in the manner IGMR 355 a describes; and by the same provision an obligatory memorial falling on a weekday of Lent is kept as an optional memorial.

rows.label: The ordinary weekdays: Advent to 16 December inclusive; Christmas Time from 2 January to the Saturday after the Epiphany; Easter Time from the Monday after the Octave of Easter to the Saturday before Pentecost inclusive; the weekdays in Ordinary Time

same_celebration.what: Mary, the Holy Mother of God

saturday_office.why: The Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary is an optional memorial and not a rank, and its condition - a Saturday in Ordinary Time on which no obligatory memorial occurs - is one the page can state but not resolve against a particular calendar. It is named at the step and never asserted.

source_advisory: This file states which norm governs a decision. It does not state what was celebrated anywhere. The universal calendar is the floor and not the answer: a national, diocesan, religious and church calendar is laid over it, the Ascension, the Body and Blood of Christ and the Epiphany sit on a Sunday only where the competent authority has actually decided it, and the competent territorial calendar or Ordo controls. Nothing here is an occurrence witness.

unsettled.what: two candidates that land on the same place
unsettled.why: the table orders within several places - and at place 12 it does not order at all, because NUALC 14 leaves the choice to the celebrant. Where two candidates tie below place 12 the derivation stops and says the day is not settled here; where they tie at place 12 it says what NUALC 14 says: one may be kept and the rest are omitted.
the article that states the one-oration rule directly has not been read in a witness here. The count is stated from NUALC 60 and IGMR 355 a instead.

unsettled.what: the mass choice IGMR 363 leaves open on a weekday in Ordinary Time
unsettled.why: it is a real choice and it is not written, because no arm of a mass_choices entry can name a base that changes with the date and no `when` can confine a choice to one season. The attempt, the two gaps and the shape the entry needs are recorded in full at implied ordinary-time-weekday, under mass_choice_not_yet_expressible; the oration scope that entry would need is declared beside it and does not choose a basis either.
